assist.exactQuestion: Acquire materially new primary or independent evidence reusable by the root owner to close source-addressed underwriting gaps.

claims.claim: Independent Zacks coverage of Varonis Q2 2026 reports $911.5M of cash, cash equivalents, short-term deposits and marketable securities at June 30, 2026; first-half free cash flow of $69.1M versus $82.7M in the prior-year period; total SaaS ARR of $726M, up 52% year over year; and SaaS ARR excluding conversions of $598.1M, up 25% year over year.
claims.materiality: This adds a materially independent analyst-origin confirmation of the transition's simultaneous SaaS growth and weaker first-half cash conversion, rather than another issuer/SEC-derived origin. Alpha can use it to test whether the active confidence assessment is sufficiently corroborated without changing numeric underwriting authority.

claims.claim: Zacks also reports management cited more than 20% SaaS ARR growth from new customers and adoption of Atlas, Interceptor and Database Activity Monitoring, while several large deals slipped into July and subsequently closed.
claims.materiality: The independent report supplies execution context around new-logo/product demand and timing risk that can be checked against the existing SaaS-transition thesis.

risks.risk: First-half 2026 free cash flow declined year over year despite strong SaaS ARR growth, so transition quality should not be inferred from ARR growth alone.

contradictions.statement: The independent report supports the existing packet tension: strong SaaS growth coexists with weaker first-half free-cash-flow conversion.

unknowns: The independent report relies partly on company-reported quarter metrics and does not establish customer-level churn, competitive win/loss rates or fair value.
This evidence does not itself justify changing Alpha's numeric factor, risk or confidence assessments.
recommendedNextState: Use the new Zacks origin as independent corroboration when reassessing the remaining data-confidence failure; preserve Alpha's numeric underwriting authority.

learning.failedStrategy: Additional same-origin SEC/issuer facts and current valuation context had not removed the active confidence failure.
learning.changedStrategy: Changed source class to a separate independent financial-analysis provider that corroborates both SaaS growth and cash-conversion weakness with execution context.
learning.nextLawfulAction: Alpha should determine whether this genuinely separate origin materially improves corroboration enough to close dataConfidenceEvidence; if not, seek customer/industry evidence rather than another financial-summary provider.
